methods.name: Automated landslide detection model (ALDM)
methods.summary: The ALDM is an unsupervised method that uses LiDAR-derived DEMs to identify landslide-prone terrain based on surface roughness. It involves calculating slope, performing focal statistics (variety function) to quantify roughness, and applying image processing techniques (binarization, noise removal via bwareaopen, and morphological closing) in MATLAB to delineate landslide extents.
methods.verbatim: The purpose of this study is to present a simple, new methodology that can be implemented with readily available tools and datasets without the need to supervise the analysis after the parameters regarding landslide morphology are defined for that region. This methodology is referred to as automated landslide detection model (ALDM).

reproducibility_assessment: The landslide inventory and other input datasets are mentioned but lack direct links, and the custom ALDM code is not provided via any repository or persistent link.
